clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says he doesn't need Viagra, sleeps through the night without getting up, and calls his own prostate perfect at his age.

His explanation isn't genetics. It's four everyday questions he keeps asking himself: what you eat, what you drink, what you breathe, and how you rest.

He credits a researcher he calls Dr. Morta with naming these the Six Essentials for Health, the basics behind everything else he teaches.

Simple on paper, but most people can't answer all four honestly. Which one would you fail first?

clips.start_words: A past member of the FDA
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau cites a claim from a former FDA commissioner: drugs, taken exactly as directed, cause more deaths a year than the conditions they're prescribed for.

His example: Tylenol. A headache or a sore back won't end a life on its own, but Kevin's source ties the drug itself to around 2,000 deaths a year, used exactly as the label says.

His bigger point: many conditions people medicate daily, like psoriasis, were never life-threatening to begin with.
